decisions.reason: As an incremental, modular evolution of the established BASIC 518 screen, it fits the firm's existing knowledge base very closely and the reported further development indicates learning and improvement rather than a candidate for exit.

The mobile high-speed flail shredder sits in the firm's core shredding competence and the 2019 Stage V update shows the firm could absorb regulatory and engineering knowledge into the product line, supporting continuation.

The mobile high-speed grinder is closely related to the firm's mobile processing machinery and its move from a mention in 2018 to its own page in 2019 suggests growing internal commitment and capacity to refine it commercially.

The stationary single-shaft pre-shredder builds directly on the firm's strong shredding know-how, and the 'new CERON generation' positioning plus concrete application evidence indicate high absorptive capacity and strong prospects for retention.
